conventions.convention: Potentials use whole-system SI quantities: entropy in J/K, amounts in mol, energy in J, temperature in K, volume in m³, pressure in Pa, and chemical potentials in J/mol. Heat capacities are whole-system values.

Each Legendre potential is a local natural-coordinate function only where the corresponding conjugate-coordinate map has a C1 inverse between open neighborhoods. The volume conjugate is −p, giving plus pV in H and G.

Euler and Gibbs–Duhem require local degree-one homogeneity of the same fixed-tag energy function. General tagged scaling alone does not supply this; the designated common-law branch supplies it through entropy transport and local inverse uniqueness.
Isentropic compressibility is −V⁻¹(∂V/∂p) at fixed total entropy and every amount, only on a valid local (s,p,n) inverse chart.

Reservoir potentials use fixed external T0 and p0, not necessarily the system's endpoint temperature and pressure. They equal the natural Helmholtz or Gibbs potentials only at matching endpoint intensives.

Useful work is positive for energy delivered to the entropy-neutral work store; work on the system is −p0 ΔV − Wout. Equality in the work bound requires zero total entropy production but does not assert an attainable protocol.
The closed model loop traverses the hotter isotherm toward increasing volume and the colder isotherm toward decreasing volume; work on the system is −∮p dV.

load_bearing.statement: On their respective valid charts define H=U+pV, F=U−Ts, G=U−Ts+pV, and Ω=U−Ts−Σμj nj, with natural coordinates (s,p,n), (T,V,n), (T,p,n), and (T,V,μ), respectively.
For C2 f(u,z) on an open domain, if (u,z)↦(Du f(u,z),z) has the stated C1 local inverse (x,z)↦(g(x,z),z), then f̂(x,z)=f(g(x,z),z)−x·g(x,z) is C2 and d f̂=−g·dx+Dz f(g(x,z),z)·dz.
On the stated valid local inverse charts the potentials are C2, with dU=T ds−p dV+Σμj dnj, dH=T ds+V dp+Σμj dnj, dF=−s dT−p dV+Σμj dnj, dG=−s dT+V dp+Σμj dnj, and dΩ=−s dT−p dV−Σnj dμj.

For the named C2 potentials on their open natural-coordinate charts, every pair of conjugate coefficients in its exact differential has equal cross derivatives, with unlisted natural coordinates held fixed.
On an open C2 Helmholtz chart at fixed composition, with T>0, V>0, the required local (T,p,n) response inverse, and κT>0, Cp−CV=TVαp²/κT.

For a local C2 positive-temperature energy representation and an open subdomain satisfying the stated same-tag local homogeneity hypothesis, U=Ts−pV+Σμj nj and s dT−V dp+Σnj dμj=0 throughout that subdomain.
If C is open, f:C→R is C1, and each x has a nondegenerate interval Jx⊂(0,∞) containing 1 on which λx∈C and f(λx)=λf(x), then f(x)=Df(x)[x]=Σxj ∂j f(x). The point 1 may be an endpoint of Jx.

concerns.concern: Several displayed species derivatives explicitly hold the whole vector n fixed while differentiating one of its components, for example “T_{n_j}|_{s,V,n}=μ_{j,s}|_{V,n}”. The introductory convention makes the intended relation recoverable, but the displayed fixed-variable list should use n_{k≠j} on the side differentiated in n_j. The same notation occurs in the U, H, F, and G bullets.

Step 1.1 invokes the supplier's dH=T ds+V dp on its valid enthalpy natural chart, but this theorem assumes Helmholtz and (T,p,n) response charts, without an (s,p,n) inverse. Those hypotheses need not provide an enthalpy natural chart, particularly when Cp=0, which this statement allows. The claimed identity remains valid: derive dH directly from H=U+pV and the energy differential, or from H=G+Ts, on the available chart. That short derivation is currently implicit.

seams_checked.note: Checked the entropy-conjugate, response-chart, mechanical-coupling, and local-energy interfaces. The consuming text preserves SI pullbacks, positive temperature, local C2 regularity, inverse-chart hypotheses, and the draft implicit-rank supplier's C1 conclusion with a separate C2 upgrade.

The cycle page and its reservoir-cycle, engine, and refrigerator items use compatible affine bath entropy and heat/work signs. The bounds are proved from their own explicit first- and second-law bookkeeping; no stronger Legendre-potential or reservoir-minimum conclusion is attributed to this batch.

Phase definitions retain local Gibbs chart requirements. Reaction-boundary equilibrium uses the Gibbs differential only at positive amounts and supplies separate boundary premises. Clapeyron explicitly retains same-tag homogeneity, valid Gibbs charts, and the common-law branch's local-inverse and reference conventions.

The page and finite-canonical identity explicitly distinguish Fstat=mean energy−T Sstat from a macroscopic Helmholtz potential. They make no unsupported identification with this batch's Legendre functions or empirical thermodynamic measurements.
